speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. To help me understand the connection between your double vision, trouble climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness, could you tell me if these symptoms have been getting worse over time or did they start suddenly? Also, have you noticed any difficulty with swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very concerning for a neuromuscular junction disorder. To confirm this, could you tell me if you have experienced any drooping of your eyelids (ptosis), particularly in the morning? REQUEST TEST: Repetitive Nerve Stimulation

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. Based on the classic fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity, the ocular symptoms triggered by up/down gaze, and the confirmatory findings on Repetitive Nerve Stimulation showing decreased response, the diagnosis is Myasthenia Gravis. I will request a Chest CT to check for an associated thymoma or thymic hyperplasia, which is common in this condition.
